question.text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the most basic oxide of vanadium among <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math>' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></math> is____B.M. (Nearest integer)

solution.text:
V2O3 is the most basic oxide among the given oxides.

In V2O3, Vanadium is in +3 oxidation state

V3+⇒Ar3d24s0

So, 2 unpaired electrons are there,

Its magnetic moment is equal to μ=nn+2 BM=22+2 BM

=2.83 BM ≃ 3 BM

(n= number of unpaired electrons)
